newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's reserve money jumps 24 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Romania's reserve money jumps 24 pct in July.

text.p: The daily average of Romanian reserve money rose by 24 percent to 9.79 trillion lei last month after a 6.2 percent increase in June, central bank (BNR) data showed on Tuesday.
Reserve money, also known as monetary base or high-powered money, includes cash in circulation and in vaults and banks' minimum reserves.
The upswing in reserve money was triggered by a jump in banks' minimum reserves, which soared to a daily average of 2.71 trillion lei in July from 1.59 trillion the previous month, BNR data showed.

Bankers said the upsurge in banks' minimum reserves was prompted by an overliquid money market during July following BNR dollar purchases which flooded the market with leu funds. They also said banks' lending activity remained subdued after months of tough monetary policies.
In a bid to mop up excess leu funds, the BNR decided in mid-July to raise the rate for minimum reserve on banks' leu deposits to 10 percent from a previous 7.5 percent.
The BNR also drained funds from the money market by taking leu deposits from local banks, mopping up a daily average of 1.31 trillion lei in July, according to latest data.
BNR data also showed the daily average of currency outside banks grew by 12.5 percent to 6.77 trillion lei in July.
